what: On the dark panel’s upper right, a big droplet sphere (radius .82, at screen-ratio×.75) floats, rippling slowly with reflection noise, and once the cursor first moves, a tail of 15 small spheres following the cursor (big in front, smaller toward the back, follow .35) grows by .05 per frame and melts stickily into the big sphere (smooth-min k 7). Drawn on a single three.js plane with our raymarching shader (16 steps), mixing two layers of reflection-direction noise raised to the 7th power so only purple and white edge light flashes in the dark. Resolution .5×, time ×2. Drawn only while the panel is on screen

options.x · y · r: Large sphere position · radius (short side of screen = 2), default 1.25 (or screen ratio×.75, whichever is larger) · .25 · .82
options.m-x · m-y · m-r: Narrow screen (768 or less · portrait) large sphere, default .65 · −.15 · .8
options.--fx-tint-a · --fx-tint-b: Two reflection noise colors, default a deep purple made from the accent · 41% of the stage text color
options.[data-fx-part=canvas]: Canvas to draw on — created if missing

note: THREE is loaded first as a global (_vendor/three@0.174.0 build/three.cjs via a window.exports trick). The cursor is read from the whole document, so it keeps following even when text on the panel covers it. With reduced motion, only the big sphere is drawn once
